DLS is more robust than DCS, but that the latter is more sensitive and can be used for larger particles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SOPs should be developed by expert laboratories and that they should be tested by independent laboratories for their robustness.
the DLS SOPs were found to be sufficiently robust to allow for a wide range of instrument types to be used and that they can be used also for measurements in biological fluids.

SOPs are essential for obtaining comparable and reliable particle size data, but that the development of SOPs needs to be performed in a systematic manner, and that the verification of these SOPs needs to involve a larger number of participants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of standardized SOPs is a prerequisite for reliable and comparable nanoparticle size data.
the development of SOPs is an iterative process and that the development of a single SOP that is applicable to all measurement systems is unrealistic.
the use of SOPs can lead to a substantial increase in the reliability and comparability of particle size data.
